classification_unit: overlapping fact or issue occurrence unless case_count is stated

MISSING_ATOMIC_FACT.pattern: An independently represented property was omitted, including one deliberate duplicate-label diagnostic occurrence.

OVER_BROAD_FACT.pattern: A clause-sized topical phrase or whole missing/negative statement was treated as one fact.

MULTIPLE_FACTS_MERGED.pattern: No unambiguous multi-property merge remained; current decomposition defects were omissions or property misassignment.

NEGATIVE_INFORMATION_EMITTED_AS_POSITIVE.pattern: A statement denying the existence of an issue was emitted as affirmative notice metadata.

MISSING_INFORMATION_EMITTED_AS_POSITIVE_.pattern: The topic named by a missing-data statement was treated as evidence that the corresponding fact exists.

RAW_VALUE_TOO_BROAD.pattern: Semantically related facts retained subject, object, or sentence context beyond the minimal fact expression.

SOURCE_SPAN_TOO_BROAD.pattern: The span was internally grounded but included event or sentence context beyond the expected literal fact.

WRONG_NORMALIZED_VALUE.pattern: Text was echoed instead of the canonical representation, a property was assigned the wrong value, or an unsupported numeric value was invented.

WRONG_ASSERTION_MODE.pattern: One ordinary explicit value was marked inferred; one deliberate profile-specific diagnostic expected inferred from identical literal text.

CANDIDATE_ISSUE_FALSE_NEGATIVE.pattern: Misses concentrated in missing-information language, bare canonical token bundles, and preliminary issue-only diagnostics.

CANDIDATE_ISSUE_FALSE_POSITIVE.pattern: Wage-topic or token-position cues caused an issue to be emitted without the expected supported intent.
